Retrieve the Outlier Summary Table from an Object

Source: R/flagQC.R
getOutlierSummary.Rd

Returns the table flagQC() recorded when it flagged the object: one row per metric per group, holding the thresholds that were applied and how many cells each one caught. It is a plain data frame, so it can be sorted, subset, written to CSV or joined against a sample sheet like any other.

Usage

getOutlierSummary(obj)

Arguments

obj

A Seurat object that has been through flagQC().

Value

A data frame with one row per metric per group. See the Value section of flagQC() for what each column means. Aborts if the object has never been flagged, rather than returning NULL for a caller to trip over.

Details

The table is a record of what was flagged, not a live view of the object. It is written when flagQC() runs and is not recalculated afterwards, so cell counts describe the object as it stood at that moment. Subsetting the object does not update them – which is the point, since the whole reason to keep the table is to be able to say afterwards how many cells were dropped and why.

Repeated flagQC() calls accumulate into one table, so an object flagged on counts globally and then on mitochondrial content per sample yields a single table describing both. Rows for a flag column that was overwritten are replaced rather than duplicated, so every row corresponds to a metadata column that is actually present.

See also

flagQC(), which writes this table, and diagnoseQC(), which calculates the metrics it describes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
seurat <- diagnoseQC(seurat, organism = "mmu")
seurat <- flagQC(
    seurat,
    metrics  = c(nCount_RNA = "lower", pctMito = "higher"),
    group_by = "Ident"
)

qc <- getOutlierSummary(seurat)
qc

# the thresholds that were actually applied, per sample
qc[, c("metric", "group", "lower", "upper", "n_lower", "n_upper")]

# which samples lose the most cells, and to which metric?
qc[order(-qc$pct_flagged), c("metric", "group", "n_flagged", "pct_flagged")]

# groups no threshold could be estimated for
qc[is.na(qc$column), c("metric", "group", "n_cells")]

# keep it alongside the filtered object
write.csv(qc, "qc/outlier_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} # }
